human_tolerance.notes: A ubiquitous feeder and nesting-box bird in North American suburbs; it will approach a feeder or hand, and uses nest boxes readily. human_tolerance thresholds are authored judgement for suburban-lot placement.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Pairs and winter flock members hold ranges and contest dominance rank; authored from the year-round flocking and dominance behaviour.

phases.name: nesting
phases.note: Cavity nesting, a clutch of six to eight eggs and incubation of 11-14 days by the female, with the male feeding her; month boundaries are the sourced late-April to late-June nesting season.

phases.name: young
phases.note: Nestlings fledge 12-16 days after hatching and remain in the family group about a week after leaving the nest.

phases.name: caching
phases.note: Autumn and winter food caching; the hippocampus grows during the caching season, which is believed to help the bird remember its cache locations.

vocalizations.description: The clear two-note whistled song fee-bee, the first note higher than the second, given year-round from a perch and answered by other flock members.
The chick-a-dee-dee-dee call the species is named for; it warns of predators and is used by other birds in mixed winter flocks, which react when a chickadee gives it.
Chirping begging calls from nestlings in the cavity or nest box when an adult arrives with food; months and time window are authored from the April to June nesting season.

external.note: GBIF usage key 2487805 and Wikidata Q282687 confirmed from the live APIs; iNaturalist taxon id 144815 from the iNaturalist taxa API; ITIS TSN 554382 from the ITIS template in the Wikipedia article, which agrees with the ITIS search-by-scientific-name service. No NCBI taxon id is recorded because none was confirmed here; that key is optional.

common_names.note: English name from GBIF and Wikipedia. The French, German and Dutch labels are the standard names for the species in those languages from Wikipedia sitelinks; they are not independently sourced here.

conservation.note: Least Concern. Wikipedia's article is a good article and its infobox cites the IUCN status; the IUCN page itself was not used, because it is not openly licensed.

range.note: Country list from Wikipedia's stated range: from the northern United States to southern Canada and up to Alaska and Yukon, so the United States and Canada are recorded and no other country is claimed. Köppen classes are coarse authored judgement from that range and include Dfa and Dfb for the Ontario target region.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Hop along tree branches searching for food and fly between perches, as the article describes; glide is not modeled because the source does not describe gliding.

traits.nest_type.note: Nests are built in tree cavities, and nest boxes are used.

traits.perching.note: Hops along branches and perches to give the fee-bee song.

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia's 10-14 g range for both sexes; Wikidata P2067 independently gives 13 g, consistent with that midpoint.

traits.length_m.note: Judgement, and the weakest number in this record. The Wikipedia article gives no total length for this species: it documents only bill length 8-9.5 mm, tail length 58-63 mm, wing length 63.5-67.5 mm and tarsus length 16-17 mm, and its Speciesbox carries no length field either. 0.13 m is an authored estimate for a small passerine of the documented 10-14 g mass, bracketed by the documented tail length; it is not a quoted measurement, and no allow-listed source carrying a total length for Poecile atricapillus was found. traits.length_m is required by the schema, so it could not be omitted; reviewers should treat this value as a labelled estimate rather than a measurement.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Judgement, forced by the schema. The validator requires traits.wingspan_m for a species with a Fly locomotion mode, and the Wikipedia article documents no wingspan for this species (its Speciesbox carries no wingspan field either), so the value cannot be omitted. 0.18 m is an authored estimate derived from the estimated total length of 0.13 m at the roughly 1.4x wingspan-to-length ratio typical of small passerines. It is not a quoted measurement.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Wikipedia gives a maximum recorded lifespan of 12 years but says most live roughly 2.5 years; the typical figure is recorded here and the maximum is deliberately not.

traits.home_range_ha.note: Judgement: the source describes flock and pair ranges but gives no area, so 1.0 ha is an authored figure for a small garden-territory songbird.

traits.diet.note: Wikipedia says the species feeds primarily on insects and seeds, and that insects, especially caterpillars, form a large part of the diet in summer. The 0.6/0.4 split is authored from that description.

traits.social.note: The article calls the species social, states that it forms strict dominance hierarchies within its flock, and describes mixed-species flocks outside the breeding season, so Flock is the right structure. The upper group_size of 12 is authored judgement: the source describes flocks but gives no size.

traits.defense.note: The article documents the chick-a-dee-dee alarm call and its use by flock members, plus escape when disturbed at the nest; mobbing of predators is not described for this species in the source, so Flee is the conservative choice.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: extremely tolerant of people for a wild passerine, and a habitual feeder and nest-box user, so wariness is set very low.

habitat.use.note: The species lives in deciduous and mixed forests and hops along tree branches; the arboreal share is authored and the small ground share covers hopping down to cached seed and snow.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Cavity, for nesting in nest boxes or natural holes.

habitat.resources.note: Invertebrate, seed and fruit tags follow the sourced diet; cavity, perch and shrub_thicket reflect cavity nesting, branch-perching foraging and winter flock cover; the summer fruit months are authored.

habitat.requires.note: Judgement for the behavior program: a hopping songbird needs at least one nearby perch in the simulation.

habitat.suitability.note: Judgement from the habitat description - deciduous and mixed woodland, wooded suburbs and feeders - with curves authored for suburban-lot placement.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Nest boxes, feeders and willingness to approach people; the numeric thresholds are authored judgement for simulation placement.

seasonal.strategy.note: The article calls the species nonmigratory and notes that while it normally does not migrate between habitats, irregular migration and dispersal may occur in winter, so ActiveYearRound is the honest fit.

seasonal.phases.note: Nesting season from late April to late June, six to eight eggs, incubation 11-14 days, fledging 12-16 days after hatching and a family group for about a week after leaving the nest all come from Wikipedia, as does autumn caching and the winter flock period. Territorial and flocking month boundaries are authored.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Egg and juvenile stages follow the sourced incubation of 11-14 days and fledging at 12-16 days; duration and scale are simulation judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for bt-perching-songbird-v1: low flee distance for a feeder-tame species, branch-hop insect foraging, the fee-bee as song and chick-a-dee-dee as alarm, and an April to June cavity-nesting window.

vocalizations.fee_bee.note: Wikipedia names the fee-bee song explicitly.

vocalizations.chick_a_dee_dee.note: Wikipedia names the chick-a-dee-dee-dee call, gives it as the source of the species' common name, and records other species reacting to it in mixed flocks.

vocalizations.begging.note: Judgement: nestling begging is not described in the source article, so this call is modeled from the documented cavity-nesting period. Season months, time window and cooldown are authored.

look.note: Wikipedia describes a black cap and bib, white cheeks, white underparts with buff-coloured flanks, an unstreaked greenish grey back, slate grey tail and wings, a black beak and legs and dark brown irises. Palette and block proportions are authored judgement for a stylised model.
